To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamically generated axial-vectors are stable with respect to their interactions with the pseudoscalars and the vectors, and that the light-quark-mass dependence of the dynamically generated axial vectors can be understood in terms of the light-quark masses dependence of the pseudoscalers and vector mesons.

(i) the dynamically generated axial vector mesons are stable in the unitary chiral perturbation approach, (ii) the $f_1$ and $h_1$ mesons are stable for pion masses below 500 MeV, (iii) for the $b_1$ meson the stability depends on the light-quark masses, and (iv) the $a_1$ and the $K_1$ mesonic states are unstable for all pion masses
the scattering lengths of $K_1$ and $a_1$ are large and positive, and that the $K_1$, $b_1$, and $h_1$ are dynamically generated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: - The interaction of the pion, the vector mesons $\rho$, $K^\ast$, $\phi$, and the axial-vector mesons with the light quark masses of $n_f=3$ and $n_f=4$, respectively.
the interaction of the pseudoscalar mesons and vector mesons.
the interaction kernel of the pseudoscalar and vector mesons, which are the fundamental degrees of freedom of the chiral Lagrangians.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the unitary chiral perturbation, the axial-vector mesons are dynamically generated, and the scattering lengths are in the right ballpark.
the dynamically generated axial vector states are not significantly affected by the interactions with the pseudoscalar mesons and the vector meson.
the unitarized chiral perturbative calculation is consistent with lattice QCD results and that the unitarization is an important ingredient in the description of the axial-vector meson sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scattering lengths and poles of the axial-vector states are not sensitive to the pion mass in the range $m_{\pi} = 200-500$ MeV.
the dynamically generated axial vector mesons are stable and robust, with a slight dependence on the quark mass.
all the dynamically generated axial vector mesons are stable in the unitarized chiral perturbative framework with the lattice QCD input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the chiral limit, the dynamically generated states are not sensitive to the light-quark masses.
the dynamically generated axial vector states are not very sensitive to the pion mass.
the axial-vector states are not sensitive to the pion mass dependence of the vector mesons, which is in contrast to the pion-pion scattering.
